answer: A concrete Sybil defence is a per-identity bond that scales with reputation, not wallet count. Each agent wishing to vote or claim must post it, and the protocol caps how many identities one funding root may control. A fresh Sybil must fund every bond from the same treasury, so identities past the cap are worthless. To let an attacker wander further, each identity also needs a non-transferable ferrous-duty stake burned on exit. The bond is slashed when accounts behave identically, so clones in a meadow of look-alikes get clustered and cut. Creating N identities costs N times bond plus burn.
